scope: Phase10 module selection, retention, pinned identity span checking, bounded physical copy, and diagnostic-only parser hook. UNVERIFIED bytes are not published; authentication and a trusted mount are not implemented or approved by this review.
hash_semantics: SHA256 of raw on-disk bytes, not newline-normalized text. Supporting files were reviewed only as needed for the scoped integration, not as a whole-kernel audit.

checks.reason: The only production copy call retains an owned exact descriptor from accepted inventory. RAM containment, kernel/growth exclusion and metadata/module overlap rejection precede copying. Numeric addresses are not treated as authenticated provenance; the loader/firmware RAM contract and single-owner boot safety requirements remain explicit. The bounded destination is kernel-owned and disjoint.

checks.area: pins and map lifetime across heap growth
checks.reason: All loader reservations become nonusable frame records before page-table allocation and become permanent page-rounded pins. The checker requires every covered page to be pinned and currently identity-translated. Its shared PageMap borrow ends with a scalar boolean before destination allocation can grow the heap and mutably access PAGE_MAP. Growth is restricted to the excluded window; pinned mappings cannot be unmapped or overwritten through the mapping API.

Labels are inline fixed-size values; inventory module count and string scans are bounded. Payload length is checked before mapping inspection or allocation and limited to 256 KiB with fallible reserve. Parser index allocation and entry count are bounded. The hook retains neither archive nor bytes beyond the diagnostic match; archive metadata drops before the owned byte buffer. No frame guard or PageMap reference spans these allocations or drops.

checks.area: duplicate and invalid labels fail closed
checks.reason: Selection compares the entire owned label exactly. Empty, oversized, control-containing and non-ASCII names are ineligible without prefix truncation; physical validation still reaches the bounded terminator or rejects inventory. Two exact labels return ambiguity independently of loader order; main performs no module copy for ambiguity. Existing test source covers these cases, but was not executed in this review.

Rejected physical inventory records the first boot error and closes the persistent-storage gate. Selection ambiguity and copy/archive rejection remain diagnostic import failures, preserving kernel-owned RAMFS recovery without publishing module content. They intentionally do not convert accepted inventory into a storage rejection. Existing independent owned-media gates remain in place; no format or trusted /system mount is introduced by this hook.

verification.method: static source and integration-path review, including existing test source inspection
verification.reason_tests_not_run: Only the review JSON write is authorized. Building or running the harness can create other files. No QEMU was launched and no existing process was disturbed.
verification.source_hash_recheck: Parent should compare reviewed_source_sha256 with the current working tree before relying on this verdict.

limitations: This is not runtime proof of real physical RAM backing, allocator exhaustion, paging behavior or guest boot acceptance.
Safety depends on truthful loader/firmware RAM backing and the existing single-CPU, non-mutating-IRQ boot model; numeric pins alone do not authenticate source provenance.
Digest trust, namespace publication, trusted /system attachment and release acceptance remain outside this diagnostic-only slice.
